summary: sherpy CLI exfiltrates host OS information to a hardcoded Telegram bot via a compiled Rust extension
details: The `sherpy` console_script entry point unconditionally invokes three functions from a shipped Rust extension `sherpy/_core.cpython-314-darwin.so`: `_core.osi()` (OS/host information collection) followed by `_core.send_tg_ar()` and `_core.send_tg_trt()` (Telegram transmission). The Rust SBOM confirms the binary links `teloxide` (Telegram Bot API client), `reqwest` (HTTP), and `dirs` (home/config path discovery). The CLI accepts no arguments, reads no configuration file, and consults no environment variables, so the Telegram bot token and destination chat are hardcoded inside the compiled binary and the installer has no way to configure or opt out of the transmission. All executable logic lives inside a 10.8 MB Mach-O extension; the Python surface is an empty `__init__.py`/`__main__.py` and a 418-byte `cli.py` dispatcher shipping no source, which conceals the destination host, bot token, and exact collected fields from static inspection. The package summary ("Python CLI backed by a Rust engine") does not disclose Telegram transmission, and Russian-language error strings such as "Ошибка при send_tg_ar" reference the send functions directly.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
